actual_scope: At p=19, beta0=-1/2, bandwidth 2, and t_i=i, do the eigenvalues of Q = I - p^{-20} H* H on the normalized Schur section lie in [0, 1 - p^{-40}]?
scope_change_reason: Both 2-norms of this normalized section are strictly below 19^10. The named next step is the comparison of p^{-20}*(1226/625)^2 with 1 and p^{-20}*(100/319)^2 with p^{-40}.
bottleneck_link: FINE-PRIME.md places the eigenvalues of Q = I - p^{-20} H* H in [0, 1 - p^{-40}] once both 2-norms are at most p^10. On this section those comparisons hold, so the eigenvalues lie strictly inside (0, 1 - p^{-40}).
stop_rule: Stop once the two power comparisons imply the eigenvalue interval. Do not form Q and do not estimate the polynomial inverse.
evidence: research/gaussian-origin-q-eigenvalues shows p^{-20}*(1226/625)^2 < 1 and p^{-20}*(100/319)^2 > p^{-40}. Every eigenvalue is therefore strictly above 0 and strictly below 1 - 19^{-40}.

open_questions.question: On this section, is the error of p^{-20} sum_{j < J} Q^j H* at most p^{10} exp(-p^2) for J = ceil(p^{42})?
open_questions.why_it_matters: FINE-PRIME.md uses that tail, after the eigenvalue interval, to replace the old locality scale. The interval is now checked here; the tail is not.
open_questions.first_step: With r = 1 - p^{-40} and J = ceil(p^{42}), compare p^{-20} * r^J / (1-r) * (1226/625) with p^{10} exp(-p^2) by rational bounds. Do not form Q.
